how: The starter proposed a character mark, tried an anchor location, and was later credited for initiating the effort.
Recruitment combined a dedicated call, wider outreach proposals, and moderator promotion through a sticky.
A bare offer of help received a brief acknowledgment without asking for anything back.
Limited hands explicitly shaped a small template that could be extended after the first character.
The same starter progressed from proposing the mark to issuing the dedicated call for help.
The dedicated call received an explicit offer to help, and subsequent participants reported building and maintenance.
Bare joining occurs, but an acceptance can also volunteer an episode-delay explanation without being a refusal.
A question about finding the work in the final canvas received a landmark-based explanation.
Sleep and worry about future erasure are visible, but no concept establishes quitting from strain or repairing a quarrel between builders.
The room adopted a character template and subsequently proposed correcting its maker's mistaken hair colour.
Builders reported dimensions, continued labour, and qualified completion of the trio.
Coordinates, dimensions, colour instructions, and updated templates supplied a common placing plan.
Few available builders made a small, incrementally extensible template preferable to a larger initial design.
The posted template was accepted as workable but remained open to correction rather than permanently settling every design choice.
Builders completed reference hats before adjusting the shared design's position.
Participants reported cheering in an existing chat and proposed a build channel that others could join.
A proposal to open a channel and reported chat support do not establish completed migration or the decisions made within that channel.
Participants fitted work around sleep and other maintenance commitments, while an episode delay gave one person time to join.
Builders were told to refresh before placing because their canvas view did not always update.
A stale canvas view made refreshing a prerequisite to placing the shared plan against current pixels.
Discussion of neighbouring automation constraining the build must remain distinct from evidence that the focal room adopted machine placement.
Neighbouring bots and human labour are documented, while undisclosed local bot use remains unresolved.
Maintenance under pressure is visible, but no coded passage establishes a local transition from upkeep to automation.
Retrospective leadership and moderator promotion cannot establish the global frequency claim or resolve whether this room formally appointed its leaders.
Private contact with a neighbour is documented as diplomacy rather than a stated effort to hide plans or infiltrate a rival.
Members volunteered upkeep, handed maintenance to teammates when sleeping, and recounted last-minute defence.
The completion comment explicitly turned from the witches being up to keeping them maintained until closure.
Participants attributed repeated hair resets to neighbouring bots and a wrong colour to the template maker's own memory.
Repeated resets show that permission from a representative does not establish effective communication to keepers or isolate ignorance as the cause of every overwrite.
Builders accepted losing optional hair pixels while preserving the rest of the trio.
Members negotiated tiny overlaps, permission for a border row, and mutual non-expansion.
Members contacted neighbours privately, reported permissions, and identified an ambassador.
Neighbours promised non-expansion and later apologised for damage they had not prevented.
Participants offered maintenance for assistance, promised future help, and thanked accommodating neighbours.
The host relation was limited to a few hair pixels for which a neighbouring group granted an explicit allowance.
A neighbour apologised for inability to control all its fans, and the reply accepted that limit on coordinating placers.
The pixel allowance was followed by an apology about uncontrolled fans and acceptance of that limit, without rejection of the agreement.
Accepting an apology preserved neighbourly goodwill after uncontrolled placers defeated the promised pixel allowance.
A proposal to negotiate overlap addressed interference at the shared edge while builders continued fitting the trio.
Boundary negotiation overlapped fitting and building the trio before its completion announcement.
The ambassador's non-expansion assurance received a reply promising reciprocal respect for the boundary.
Offers of reciprocal upkeep are explicit, but receipt of additional hands caused by those offers is not established.
An overlap allowance elicited a promise of future assistance, while an ambassador's approach elicited an offer to maintain the neighbour's logo.
A participant explicitly identified with the adjoining fandoms and enjoyed working on their shared canvas section.
Participants proposed anchor locations and arranged the hats to fit or shift within available space.
Location choice and fitting are visible, but an intervening squished attempt prevents classifying the change between anchors as demonstrably before any loss.
A squished attempt and a different anchor do not preserve a decision weighing fighting against relocation after defeat.
Scarcity explicitly explains the smaller template, but its causal role in changing anchor locations remains unresolved.
Friendly neighbours and cross-group chat contact do not establish a coalition beyond the bilateral relationships recorded.
Maintenance and bilateral contact cannot establish a threat-driven decision to join a coalition.
Complaints about bot power and acceptance of lost pixels do not establish an exchange debating whether covering art is fair.
Requests for overlap and mutual non-expansion promises supply no coded attack call by this room.
Military metaphors and celebration do not establish a contest conducted in talk against a named rival.
Fandom representation and friendly neighbour exchanges leave a pre-existing quarrel carried into the canvas undocumented.
No coded attack call supplies a prior tie naming a rival, so this room cannot test that conditional claim.
Recruitment reaches building and negotiation in the concepts without documenting a subsequent call to attack.
Boundary restraint is visible, but the record supplies no initiating attack call against which to test refusal.
The overlap proposal does not identify an attack call as the reason for negotiation.
Celebratory soldier language cannot test whether an attack caused a rivalry in talk.
Participants celebrated completion, credited starters and helpers, and expressed enjoyment of shared work.
Celebrating survival remained compatible with acknowledging lost details of the preferred design.
Participants marked the platform's end, reported survival and overwritten overlaps, and located the work on the finished canvas.
Qualified completion was followed by an announcement of historical presence and explicit credit to contributors.
Celebration and recording coexist, but original publication times cannot date survival edits or establish that celebration caused preservation.
A neighbouring participant visited to congratulate the room and recall their cross-group work, without claiming new fandom membership.
End-marking and recollection of lost overlap do not show a dispute about cleaning or correcting a preserved canvas version.
Friendly thanks and enjoyment after closure do not establish a continuing project, a new canvas, or a decision to preserve a collective.
Remembrance is documented, but no decision links it to a continuing project.
Credit to local helpers and pride in the mark do not establish outreach to creators, companies, or press.
Moderators increased a recruitment call's visibility by stickying it.
Stickying promoted participation, while no concept establishes containment rules, a canvas flood, or moving all canvas talk elsewhere.
Calls and supportive moderation are visible, but the proposed intervening flood and resulting containment remain undocumented.
The coded build and episode-delay explanation do not establish a local April Fools takeover framing the call.
Supportive moderator promotion does not show resentment of canvas posts causing members to damage their own mark.
A build channel proposed inside an existing community does not establish a new canvas-born faction.
Character representation and multi-fandom enjoyment leave a broader collective performance of lore, ideology, or colour faith undocumented.
Military metaphors alone do not demonstrate a new canvas joke taken up and maintained by the room.
Profanity about interference does not establish a dispute over offensive speech or a shared action against hate symbols.
